summary: Rabun Bald summit fire tower in Chattahoochee NF, Georgia; USFS-run into the early 1970s, cab replaced by a wooden platform; 1922 and 1930s build dates conflict.

facts.design: Stone base with a metal-framed glass cab, later replaced by a railed wooden observation platform
facts.status_note: Fire cab removed after service; stone base and wooden observation platform remain

access.note: Reached on foot by the Rabun Bald Trail; no source gives gate, hours or climbing rules for the platform

visit.trail_note: Round trip 4.2 miles with about 1,100 ft of climb (Chattooga Conservancy) or 5.8 miles (Wikipedia)

events.note: Atlanta Constitution item, quoted by Forest Lookouts: a Forest Service tower just completed on the extreme summit, fourteen feet with a glass house. Not reconciled with the 1930s accounts.
NHLR and Chattooga Conservancy date the first tower to the 1930s (decade only), built by Nick Nicholson
Wikipedia says the USFS operated the tower until the early 1970s; year is approximate

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 4,698 ft (1,432 m) and Wikipedia 4,696 ft (1,431 m). The Chattooga Conservancy's 4,969 ft is far off the other two and was not used.

notes_for_editor: Build date is disputed: a November 1922 Atlanta Constitution item (via Forest Lookouts) describes a 14-ft Forest Service tower on the summit, while NHLR and Chattooga say the first tower dates to the 1930s. The story reports both and does not reconcile them. Trail length also disagrees (4.2 vs 5.8 mi round trip) and is reported as such. No staffing, fire or NRHP sources were found. The YCC conversion has no date in any source, so it is not in events. Access is inferred from trail-based public visits; no gate or climbing rule was found.
